edbDesc: The splitting of a spectral line into several components in the presence of a static magnetic field. The Zeeman effect is very important in applications such as nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy, electron spin resonance spectroscopy, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and Mössbauer spectroscopy. It may also be utilised to improve accuracy in Atomic absorption spectroscopy.
title: Zeeman Effect
pickWhy: The deck's light-and-magnetism card is Zeeman's 1896 splitting of spectral lines in a magnetic field.
